## `elanous schedule`

Schedule/cron CRUD (keeps the registry, crontab and memory consistent). --json for programmatic use.

```text
elanous schedule [options] [command]
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| `list [options]` | List all cron jobs (category filter) |
| `inspect [options] <id>` | Details + recent deliveries |
| `runs [options] <id>` | Schedule run history (newest first) |
| `create [options]` | New cron job (cron expression + command). Automatic backup; adds cd, bun and logging. |
| `update [options] <id>` | Change a cron time |
| `enable [options] <id>` | Enable a job |
| `disable [options] <id>` | Disable a job (commented out) |
| `delete [options] <id>` | Delete (automatic backup · recoverable). Dry-run by default · --yes to apply |
| `wrap [options] [id]` | ★ Observability wrap — wrap bun .ts cron jobs in cron-run.ts so each firing is recorded in three places (logs.db · registry · self-memory). No id = every .ts cron job. Dry-run by default · --yes to apply (automatic backup · keeps the id across unwrap · reversible) |
| `unwrap [options] [id]` | Remove the observability wrapper (reversible) — no id = every wrapped cron job. Dry-run by default · --yes to apply |
| `migrate [options] <id>` | Move to a fabric Schedule Trigger (fired by the elanous daemon). Dry-run by default · --yes to apply |
| `adopt [options] <id>` | Alias of migrate (merged when schedule-runner was retired). Dry-run by default · --yes to apply |
| `release [options] <id>` | Restore to running from crontab. Dry-run by default · --yes to apply |
| `retarget [options]` | Replace cron cd &lt;folder&gt; in bulk — the --from folder with the --to folder. Dry-run by default · --yes to apply (automatic backup). Errors if the target folder does not exist. |

## `elanous self author`

Only write a natural-language ask or an open clarification as a grounded eight-section goal file, or check an existing goal file with --lint.

```text
elanous self author [options] [ask...]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--cwd <path>` | Repository root to ground the goal in and write it under docs/goals/ (default: "&lt;current directory&gt;") |
| `--lint <goalFile>` | Check a goal file read-only; cannot be combined with other author arguments |
| `--print-template` | Print the canonical goal section skeleton and required levels read-only; cannot be combined with other author arguments |
| `--inspect-decision-signal <text>` | Check right away whether the verdict-signal marker matches the release marker pattern; writes no goal |
| `--inspect-invariant <text>` | Check right away the invariant markers, their parsing and the grounding evidence in the actual repository; writes no goal |
| `--inspect-boundary <text>` | Check right away the boundary markers and their parsing; writes no goal |
| `--inspect-artifact-launch <goalFile>` | Check right away the goal document's optional deliverable launch declaration; writes no goal |
| `--inspect-test-scenario <scenarioFile>` | Check right away a test scenario document's deliverable kind and live-check contract; writes no goal |
| `--inspect-target-paths <text>` | Check right away the target-path hint on the first non-empty line of the ask; writes no goal |
| `--parent-goal-file <path>` | Repository-relative path of the parent goal document that produced this goal |
| `--parent-question-id <id>` | ID of the parent goal's open question that produced this goal |
| `--from-clarification <goalFile#questionId>` | Fill in the ask and parent source automatically from an open clarification |
| `--supersedes <goalFile>` | Inherit the GoalId of an earlier goal document and record a Superseded-By back link |
| `--root-intent <text>` | Single-line root purpose to record for a new root, or for a legacy parent without RootIntent |
| `--goal-type <type>` | Goal type (implement, research, document, operate) |
| `--adversarial-review` | Run adversarial review of the goal decomposition regardless of the threshold |
| `--disable-adversarial-review` | Do not run adversarial review of the goal decomposition |
| `--enqueue` | Put the authored goal into the goal queue of the daemon's resident loop (needs --termination-command) |
| `--termination-command <cmd>` | Termination command to use when queueing (exit 0 means the goal is done) |
| `--termination-timeout <ms>` | Time limit for the termination command in ms (default: "5000") |

## `elanous self entrances`

Print the list of Commander CLI entrances currently assembled

```text
elanous self entrances [options]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as structured JSON |

## `elanous self orchestrate`

Parallel self-dev — run several goals at once, each as an isolated-worktree self-implement subprocess, with a concurrency cap. Separate goals with `;;` (or one goal per argument). --concurrency sets how many jobs run at once (default 2).

```text
elanous self orchestrate [options] [goals...]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--concurrency <n>` | Jobs to run at once (default 2) |
| `--auto-merge` | Each job: merge automatically when the review is clean (passes --auto-merge to each self-implement, through the review node) |
| `--auto-review` | Label each job's PR for opt-in auto-review (passes --auto-review to each self-implement · each job judges its own eligibility · fail-safe). Labelled PRs are finished unattended by the review poller. |
| `--open-pr` | Each job: open a draft PR when the gate and review pass (passes --open-pr to each self-implement · promotion goes through the review node) |
| `--base <branch>` | Base branch for each job's PR |
| `--decompose` | Split one goal with an LLM into a dependency sub-DAG (parallel by topology, hot files serialized), then run it |
| `--substrate <kind>` | Where to run: local (default · isolated worktree) \| pod (Kubernetes Job · docker/harness image) |
| `--pod-account <name>` | pod: codex account (~/.elanous/auth.json openai-codex:&lt;name&gt; · a copy without the refresh token) · if omitted, a broker hands each Job the account with the most remaining quota |
| `--no-pod-rebuild` | pod: do not rebuild the image even if its version (elanous.commit) differs from HEAD — the measurement then measures the image's version |
| `--pod-pass-env <keys>` | pod: keys to pass from the host environment into the Pod (comma-separated) — e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY,ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (benchmark billing path) |
| `--bench-arms <spec>` | pod benchmark: clone one goal per arm, differing only in a single label line, and run them at once — "id=provider[:model][@KEY+KEY];…" (e.g. codex=openai-codex;or-kimi=openrouter:openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3@OPENROUTER_API_KEY) · refuses --auto-merge |
| `--help-all` | Show every orchestrate option |

## `elanous self parked`

Backlog of goals blocked (failed/cancelled) in the unattended self-dev loop, for batch decisions. Mark handled with --resolve <runId> --reason <reason>. --json for structured output.

```text
elanous self parked [options]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Structured output {parked, counts, displayLimit, omittedCount, population, stores, limitation} · each parked item = [{feature, status, stage?, error?, runId, branch?, updatedAt, source}] |
| `--limit <count>` | Maximum parked items to show |
| `--resolve <runId>` | Mark a parked run as handled by a person |
| `--reason <reason>` | Short reason for marking it handled |

## `elanous self-update`

Update an installed copy from a release, a checkout from a clean checkout; restart the nexus when approved · same as `elanous update` · with `--auto on`, runs every day

```text
elanous self-update|update [options]
```

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--from <checkout>` | Checkout to install (default: releases for an installed copy, the current checkout for a checkout) |
| `--version <version>` | Install this release version on an installed copy (default: latest) |
| `--restart` | Approve restarting the nexus |
| `--json` | Print the result as JSON |
| `--keep <n>` | Recent versions to keep after install (installed copy: current and previous; checkout: current and the daemon's version are protected · 0 = no cleanup) (default: "3") |
| `--alert` | Also send failures (exit≠0) as an alert — for unattended cron runs |
| `--skip-pwa-build` | Explicitly skip the PWA build before a checkout install |
| `--auto <on|off|status>` | Automatic updates — a macOS launchd agent or Linux systemd timer runs `self-update --restart --alert` every day at 04:17 (not turned on if a cron entry already runs it) |

## `elanous session`

Manage conversation sessions

```text
elanous session [options] [command]
```

| Subcommand | Description |
|---|---|
| `list [options]` | List recent sessions (empty 0msg sessions hidden by default — active kept) |
| `new` | Create a fresh session and mark it active |
| `resume <prefix>` | Load a session by full id or unique id prefix and mark it active |
| `show [options] [prefix]` | Print the messages of a session (default: active) |
| `compact [options] [prefix]` | Force-compact a session history NOW — bypasses the auto token-ratio gate and runs the full pipeline incl. Layer3 LLM summarize. External on-demand trigger (default: active session · forced by default). |
| `watch [options] [prefix]` | Live-tail a session — render new messages as they arrive (default: the most recently active session) |
| `delete <prefix>` | Delete a session (by id or prefix) |
| `purge [options]` | Bulk-delete sessions by filter (DRY-RUN by default · --apply to delete · destructive, cannot be undone) |
| `export [options] [prefix]` | Export a session transcript to a markdown file (default: active · ~/temp/elanous-transcript-&lt;stamp&gt;.md) |
| `fork [options] <prefix>` | Fork a session (copies history · records forkedFromId lineage) |
| `search [options] <query>` | Search conversation CONTENT across sessions (source / instance / telegram filters) |
| `subscribe [options] <prefix>` | Subscribe a surface to a session (concurrent multi-surface viewing) |
| `unsubscribe [options] <prefix>` | Leave a session (removes only this subscriber · other subscribers stay) |
| `subscribers [options] <prefix>` | List who is currently subscribed to a session (presence) |
| `turn <prefix>` | Show current session turn holder and FIFO wait queue (full id or unique prefix) |
| `takeover [options] <prefix>` | Request human write ownership through the session turn arbiter (full id or unique prefix) |
| `release [options] <prefix>` | Return CLI-owned session turn control to the next waiter or free state (full id or unique prefix) |
| `context <prefix>` | Deterministic self-cognition context — who is watching / where reachable (grounded) |
| `link <prefix>` | Emit a shareable @session:&lt;id&gt; deep link for cross-surface reference |
| `open <token>` | Open an @session:&lt;id&gt; deep link — resolves + shows who is watching (grounded) |

# External commands

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/reference/external-commands/

Beyond Bun and git, elanous spawns these. None are needed to boot; each gates
one capability. `elanous doctor` shows which ones this machine has, and
`elanous env profile` describes the environment it detected.

| command | used for |
|---|---|
| `git`, `bun` | everything (required) |
| `gh` | pull requests, harness base selection |
| `rg` (ripgrep) | code search — **the test suite needs it too** |
| `codex` | ACP delegate / harness implement on the codex backend |
| `claude`, `gemini`, `grok` | coding agents elanous drives in a terminal (`agent-mission --backend`) |
| `tailscale` | sharing the web app with your other devices (`nexus pwa share`) |
| `docker` | optional container runtime (for example OpenDesign previews in [Design systems](/using-elanous/design)) |
| `kubectl` | running harness work on a Kubernetes cluster |
| Chrome or Chromium | browser checks and page capture over the DevTools protocol |
| `tmux` | naming the session when the terminal UI runs inside tmux |
| `curl`, `ssh`, `rsync`, `unzip` | fetching, remote nodes, installers |
| `crontab` | scheduled missions |
| `ffmpeg`, `magick`, `sox`, `tesseract`, `chafa` | media / ad pipeline, OCR, terminal images |
| `python3` | a few skills |
| `open`, `say`, `osascript` | macOS only, and guarded by `process.platform` |

📏 A fresh WSL2 Ubuntu had **none** of `rg`, `gh`, `ffmpeg`, `zsh`, `java`,
`jq`, `codex`, `node` or `npm`. A full test run there produced 47
`Executable not found in $PATH` lines: `rg` ×31, `ffmpeg` ×4, `zsh` ×3,
`grok` ×1 (plus `gh` and `java` failures reported differently).

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/help/troubleshooting/

Messages that look like one problem and mean another.

## `No LLM provider available`

No provider could be used: nothing is signed in, or every account and fallback is used up. Run `elanous login status` and `elanous usage`; if nothing is signed in, run `elanous setup`.

## `elanous usage` says `unavailable (auth)` for codex, but runs work

`usage` reads the Codex CLI's own sign-in file, which is separate from the sign-in elanous uses. The line does not mean your credential is broken.

## The harness finished with a branch, not a pull request

The repository has no GitHub remote, or `gh` is not signed in. This is expected: elanous leaves the work on a branch you can merge. Run `gh auth login` if you want pull requests.

## On Linux the run stops with `codex app-server stdin drain timeout`

The Codex CLI itself is not installed. `elanous login openai-codex` signs elanous in, but the part that writes code starts the `codex` program. Install the Codex CLI and run `codex login` once.

## The service still runs the old version

Installing a new build does not restart a running service. `elanous nexus restart-needed` says whether it has to; `elanous self-update --restart` installs and restarts only when needed. To restart by hand:

```bash
launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/com.elanous.nexus"     # macOS
systemctl --user restart elanous-nexus                      # Linux (systemd user service)
```

Then compare `elanous --version` with the `daemonSha` in `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:31415/v1/health`.

## The service keeps restarting right after install

Look at the service's error log. If it says the web app is not built, point it at a built copy with `ELANOUS_PWA_STATIC_DIR` (see [install](/getting-started/install#known-limits)).

## Bun skips an optional dependency

On some Linux machines `bun install` silently skips an optional dependency when `TMPDIR` and Bun's cache are on different filesystems (an upstream Bun issue). Put the temporary directory on the same filesystem:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/tmp-bun && export TMPDIR=~/tmp-bun
```

## `command -v <tool>` finds nothing, but elanous works

Some tools are fetched on demand by the package manager. Check what elanous actually reports with `elanous doctor` instead of looking at `PATH`.

## A count of "0" in a report

Before trusting a "0", check that the report looked where you think it did (`elanous where`, `elanous logs --all --include-test`) and that the output was not cut off by a limit (`--limit`).

---

# FAQ

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/help/faq/

Every answer here was checked against the real CLI. Where a number could go stale, the command that measures it is given instead — run it rather than quoting a number.

## Does elanous run with no API keys at all?

**Yes.** `elanous doctor` exits 0 and names everything that is locked, in the form `<capability> — unlock with <KEY>`. Several resources also list a free fallback that works without a key.

To try it on a truly empty setup:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/empty-home /tmp/empty-cache
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=/tmp/empty-home ELANOUS_KEY_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/empty-cache \
  elanous doctor
```

Point `ELANOUS_KEY_CACHE_DIR` at an **empty** directory as well as emptying `HOME`. If you only empty `HOME`, the credential cache survives and you will see `resolved (cache)` lines, which means it did not really run with zero keys. Do not delete your real cache to test this; other work on the same machine uses it.

## What happens when my Codex (ChatGPT) quota runs out?

Automatic **account rotation is on by default**: elanous moves to the next Codex account that still has quota. Only if no account is usable does it fall back along the fallback chain. Falling back to Grok requires all three at once: no usable Codex account, `grok` in the chain, and Grok credentials present.

Do not assume the default; check your own instance:

```bash
elanous config get llm.fallbackChain
elanous usage          # remaining quota per account
```

See [providers](/models/providers) and [Codex subscription](/models/codex-subscription).

## Where do I send work to the harness?

```bash
elanous harness say "add tests for this file"   # one line from the terminal
elanous harness ask docs/goals/MY-ASK.md        # if you already wrote a goal document
```

Inside the terminal UI, use `/harness`. To list every entrance, run `elanous self entrances`.

## How big is the CLI?

Dozens of top-level commands and several hundred subcommands. Rather than trust a number here, run `elanous --help` or see [commands](/using-elanous/commands).

## Is the terminal UI the main interface?

**No.** The three-pane TUI was one stage in elanous's history. The core today is the **harness**, **PTY control** (reading and typing into live terminals), and the first principle of **observation → self-awareness → self-healing**. The TUI keeps running as one surface alongside the CLI, the NEXUS/PWA dashboard, MCP and chat channels. See [how elanous works](/concepts/architecture).

## What needs a paid service, and what breaks without it?

Much of elanous's view of the world depends on external services. `catalog/resources.yaml` records, for each resource, what still works without it in a `free_fallback` field.

Two caveats:

- An empty `free_fallback` means "not measured", not "nothing breaks". As of 2026-09-27 every resource that needs a credential has one written; in a source checkout, `bun scripts/resource-map-check.ts` lists any that do not (`emptyFreeFallbackIds`).
- The catalog only counts API keys. Dependencies that are installed binaries or browsers (the crawl skill, browser automation, Chrome/CDP) are not listed yet.

Treat only capabilities with a written free fallback as dependable without payment. `elanous doctor` shows what is unlocked on your machine.

## How many steps from install to a first change?

With a ChatGPT subscription, the first time is a few steps: run the installer, open a new shell, `elanous login openai-codex` (open the link and type the device code), answer first-time setup when you first run `elanous` (it asks for the model provider again and for an Obsidian vault path), then `elanous harness say "<what you want>"` from your project. Signing in to GitHub (`gh`) lets it open pull requests. See [install](/getting-started/install) and [quickstart](/getting-started/quickstart).

---

# 0.2.4

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-4/

PTY intelligence reaches stage two: elanous works inside Codex and Claude Code, installs a plugin from an agent's own menu, and passes one mission along several agents.

**PTY intelligence, stage two — elanous now works *inside* the coding agents' own screens.** It opens Codex or Claude Code as a real terminal app, answers the folder-trust prompt, types the mission and submits it, watches the screen, and hands the work along a chain — Codex implements, Claude Code reviews, Codex addresses the review, elanous checks the evidence and commits. It can also open an agent's plugin menu, search, check the marketplace name and install a plugin there. You can watch every driven terminal side by side in the web app and take over at any time. See [PTY intelligence](/using-elanous/pty-intelligence).

> **Beta — Elanous is provided as is (Apache-2.0) until the stable release. Get stable release news at [elanous.ai](https://elanous.ai).** Docs: [docs.elanous.ai](https://docs.elanous.ai) · Source: [ElanvitalAI/elanous](https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous)

## Highlights — stage two (inside the agent)

- `elanous agent-mission mission --backend codex --chain codex,claude,codex,elanous …` — one mission handed along agents; each hand-off carries the diff or summary, and the last step commits only after the evidence check passes.
- `--plugin <plugin>@<marketplace>` — installs the plugin from inside the agent's own `/plugins` menu (search → marketplace name check → install), then sends the mission.
- Folder-trust prompts (Codex and Claude Code) are answered on a new worktree, including a prompt that appears late.

## Highlights — stage one (the command line)

**Stage one — elanous drives terminals itself.** It checks the machine first, picks the smallest tool that can do the job (a shell one-liner before a coding agent), installs a missing tool by typing the package-manager line and proving it with a real command, reads an unfamiliar tool's official install page before choosing a safe line, clicks and scrolls in terminal apps that turn on mouse mode, and hands any `sudo` or sign-in step to you. See [PTY intelligence](/using-elanous/pty-intelligence).


- `elanous env profile` — what this machine has (OS, shell, package managers, CLIs, sign-in yes/no), read only.
- `elanous agent-mission plan "<mission>"` — which rung of the tool ladder a mission starts on, without running anything.
- `elanous research "<query>"` — several search engines at once, with the fan-out shown as it happens.
- `elanous agent-mission install-from-docs <tool> --smoke "<cmd>" [--dry-run]` — find the official install page, read it, pick a line this machine can run, install and verify. `sudo` lines and pages without a safe line go to you.
- `elanous pty mouse <ref> <col> <row>` — click or scroll in a mouse-enabled terminal app; refused when the app has not turned mouse mode on.
- Missing CLIs (`jq`, `gh`, `rg`, `ffmpeg`, `node`, `codex`) are installed by typing in the shell and checked with the smallest real job.
- The web app's Terminal shows each driven terminal side by side with a strip of what elanous just did and why; you can take over with the keyboard or mouse.

- On a credit policy, the hourly limit alert adds up the credits across your Codex accounts and their combined burn rate, and says when they will run out.

---

# 0.2.20

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-20/

## Behavior changes

- The PWA run-graph editor can start a new graph on an editable canvas: add nodes from the palette (drag or tap), connect outcome edges (ok, rework, fail), edit node properties, mark start and end nodes, check it with a separate validate button, and save it.
- The PWA run-graph editor can run a saved graph as a demo run (operator only, built-in side-effect-free recipes) and colours each node on the canvas as it runs, finishes or fails.
- In PWA chat, picking a skill from the `$` picker after typing a task now builds `/run-skill <skill> <task>` so the skill actually runs instead of sending a plain prompt.
- TUI `/help` fits its overlay on wide terminals again (adds columns before falling back to the chat log), so Esc closes it.
- `elanous retro facts --since 24h --json` lists retrospective facts from the log store: draft PR births and supersede deaths, supervisor stop reasons and task-agent outcomes (read-only).
- In the PWA graph editor, each node keeps its demo-run state on the canvas (running, done, failed) as a coloured ring and a word after the run ends.
- A harness run that ends parked now records the parked outcome by editing its single PR status comment instead of posting a second comment, so the PR author gets one notification email per PR.
- The release screen and away alerts say a gate shard is running past its plan instead of showing «0 minutes left».
- PWA chat no longer turns a multi-line message that starts with the harness trigger phrase into a one-line harness ask; it stays a normal chat turn.
- On the PWA loop activity map, a launch edge with no run edge for the same ref after 10 minutes is now labelled a ghost (ghost, no run ledger for N minutes) with a red dotted line and no moving packet, so it no longer looks like it is running.
- The PWA loop map no longer marks every launch older than 10 minutes as a ghost: the edges API now attaches the bound run id to a launch edge, and only a launch with no bound run and no same-ref run edge after 10 minutes is shown as ghost.
- The PWA release strip no longer shows a red "blocked" line for a failed node in a run whose status is done; it shows an amber "node failure reported, run finished" warning instead (running and failed runs keep the blocked line). Run-list start times carry a KST label.
- The PWA decisions screen gains a notices and opinions tab: it lists messages that seats and loops sent to the CEO inbox (read-only; the CEO cursor is not advanced), and a reply is posted to the original sender's inbox. The route `/v1/ops-board/notices` requires owner auth and answers only on localhost or tailnet hosts.
- `elanous config drift` and `elanous config explain <key>` show, read-only, which config keys differ between the production config and derived test-universe copies (counts and example paths, unreadable configs reported separately, secret values masked).
- Telegram /runs lists running harness runs like the TUI.
- When a harness PR merges, open harness sibling PRs that touch the same files are told right away: a live owning run gets one rebase-and-regate memo in its control inbox, and a PR with no live run gets the `elanous:needs-rebase` label (no PR comments, at most 10 siblings per merge).
- Sibling resync after a harness merge no longer fetches the file list of every open harness PR: already-marked PRs are skipped, branches sharing path tokens with the merged files go first, at most `harness.siblingResync.maxFetch` (default 40) file lists are fetched per merge with 6 in flight, and the summary event records files fetched, skipped counts and duration.
- Harness runs that stop (merge held, implement aborted, blocked draft PR open failed, nonzero Pod exit, or a task-launched child exiting nonzero right after launch) now append one `stop` line to the run ledger with a closed class, a one-line cause of at most 120 characters, an evidence reference and a next move; existing ledger entries, PR bodies and log events are unchanged.

Plus 73 internal changes.

# 0.2.19

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-19/

## Behavior changes

- `elanous guardian tick` and `elanous guardian compare --day <YYYY-MM-DD>` add a shadow-only cron guardian that records which scheduled jobs would run now and compares a day's expected fires with recorded runs, without running any job or touching crontab.
- `elanous tasks hand --completion <kind>` declares how a task finishes (code-pr, artifact, research-report, ops-action, content, watch-brief, decision-support); non-code tasks close on confirmation evidence instead of waiting for a merged PR.
- `elanous tasks hand --project <id> --target <dir>` points a task at a project folder that need not be a git repository (non-code completion kinds only) and launches it from that folder.
- Topics you pick at first setup now become personal watch sources, collected at 07:00 and briefed to your report channel at 08:30 by default (opt out with `watch.enabled=false`); a quiet day sends a one-line «no news today».
- The PWA release page draws the selected release run as a node flow (done, failed, now, remaining — with words as well as colours, per-node times when recorded, and gate shard progress), and tapping a node opens its full summary and log tail.
- `elanous tasks board [--project <id>] [--json]` shows a project › goal › milestone › task board built from task cards (`tasks hand --goal/--milestone`) and, read-only, the internal release checklist.
- Task cards record the run, goal and PR they led to (shown by `tasks show`), and mission advance uses a bound PR as evidence without `--pr`.
- In the TUI, `/now` shows running harness and release runs, late schedules and the current release in KST; `/decide` lists open decision cards and answers by number (irreversible categories ask for one confirm); `/help` is grouped into start · seven verbs · other; `/model 빠름|보통|깊음` picks a tier; `/status` speaks plain words by default (`--debug` for detail); Esc closes an open picker or modal first; in an isolated universe `dev --elanous` creates its own worktree when no `--cwd`/`--worktree` is given.
- TUI chat routes lookup, settings, research and scheduling questions to a quick single turn with matching tools instead of the coding goal loop.
- `elanous away on|off|status` (and Telegram `/away`) turns on away mode: while you are away every release-run node transition, gate result (introduced count and any waiver), block with the next move, and completion is sent to Telegram, with a one-line heartbeat every 60 minutes; blocks go out even in quiet hours. Telegram `/release` shows the current run and node on demand.
- The release gate's Pod shards count only the gate's own Jobs against its pool cap again, so the gate fans out instead of launching one shard at a time while goal Pods fill the cluster.

## Known issues

The following issues are known in this release.

- In the TUI, `/help` prints the help into the chat history instead of opening an overlay, so Esc does not dismiss it. Keep typing in the input line as usual; the help simply stays in the scrollback.

Plus 71 internal changes.

# 0.2.18

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-18/

## Behavior changes

- `elanous release run` now cuts each release on its own `release/<version>` branch, so work on main keeps landing while a release is being published; `elanous release resume` continues a failed release run from a repaired branch.
- `elanous release run --prerelease rc` publishes a release candidate (`<version>-rc.<n>`) to npm `next` and as a GitHub pre-release, leaving `latest` on the current stable release.
- `elanous tasks hand --mission` splits a mission into piece cards with precedence and hands the ready pieces to the task agent; `elanous tasks show <mission-id>` lists the pieces and their edges.
- `elanous tasks advance` hands the next mission piece once its predecessors' PRs are merged (evidence recorded with `--pr`/`--goal`) and proposes the cell green when every piece has landed, without changing the checklist.

Plus 93 internal changes.

# 0.2.17

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-17/

## Behavior changes

- with `harness.queue.directSay` on (default off), direct `harness say`/`ask` calls go through the seat queue (seat cap, order, same-cell refusal) and print a one-line reason; `--no-queue` is the emergency bypass.
- nested elanous launches are denied for Claude children through a strict MCP config, and nesting stops at a configurable depth cap.
- the hq-fence cron wrapper is generated by `elanous hq fence-wrapper install`, runs from the installed build instead of a stray worktree, and alerts when the fence fails.
- fix: the hq-fence cron wrapper now runs bun by the absolute path resolved at install time (cron has no PATH for bun), and writes a log line if even that bun is missing.
- every run-supervisor stop reason now maps to a named next step (harvest, decompose, self-review, human gate), recorded with the run.
- every landing path, including host-side unattended merges, now checks the operational landing freeze at one pre-merge point, and the release run's own version bump can pass an explicit freeze override.
- failed Pod runs now report the child's real stop reason (node, outcome, supervisor verdict) instead of a stray heal-loop line.
- authoring clarification questions are now self-answered in remote Pods for goal-file launches and supervisor rework passes, not only for the first say pass.
- a Pod launch that waits too long in admission or for a pool slot now logs `launch-stalled` with the measured reason, and a pool whose members can never hold the Job's memory limit fails fast (`pod-pool-unfit`) instead of waiting forever.
- Pod authoring no longer passes --author-grade to the in-Pod elanous (it rejected the flag); lite authoring is local-only for now, Pod authoring uses full until 0.2.18 reconnects it.

Plus 30 internal changes.

# 0.2.16

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-16/

## Behavior changes

- a stopped review PR's repair goal is enqueued, with a daily cap, only when harness helper repair is live; shadow still records it without launching.
- a harness run that exhausts its rework budget is now recorded as a failure and triaged by the heal loop.
- landing now refuses a change whose public files import a module the public export excludes.
- direct old entry commands now refuse with a pointer to harness say/ask, while harness-internal calls keep working.
- the steward no longer re-asks the same invalid working-backwards draft every tick, so its schedule stage stops timing out.
- a seat loop stops relaunching the same checklist cell after three attempts that never landed and asks a person instead.
- pr land --cwd now runs its checks against the tree it lands, not the directory it was launched from.
- install a dev build between releases with self-update --dev and undo it with self-update --rollback; runs record which build ran them.
- Intake digests now distinguish confirmed lens impacts from references, using note-led context and verdict-specific actions without human-decision prompts.
- codex overload now switches the child to grok from a real per-call signal, before retries are exhausted.
- `elanous brief add|list|compose` records briefing items (claim, domain, priority, deadline, evidence, source) and prints one unsent slot page without sending it.
- a GitHub App rate limit no longer parks good pull requests; release-path inspection falls back to the local diff or retries after the reset.
- release cut-branch can append fixes to an existing release branch by fast-forward only.
- self-update --dev now installs through the real installer and never points current at a version without its entry file; rollback restores matching version metadata.
- nested elanous launches stay refused under Codex children and cannot be re-allowed from inside a child.

## Known issues

The following issues are known in this release.

- Three test files still fail in the release check, the same as in 0.2.15, and do not affect what you run: `src/domains/surface-events.test.ts` (1 test), `test/provider-summary.test.ts` (1 test) and `test/grounding-seed-paths.test.ts` (4–5 tests that hit a 5-second timeout on a busy machine).
- The release check for this version re-ran only the two test shards that stalled, after fixing their causes, instead of the full suite.

## Security

- ACP Claude runs now strip API keys so they always use the subscription, and refuse to start if a key remains.

Plus 67 internal changes.

# 0.2.15

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-15/

## Behavior changes

- the harness no longer deletes files that were added to main after a run started when they are outside the run's target paths.
- `elanous release auto-start` previews the scheduled release cut within a window and, with `--apply`, starts the guarded release run (freeze or readiness changes defer instead of failing).
- `elanous hq fence-audit` lists cron jobs that write outside the HQ fence and proposes the wrapped line (no crontab changes).
- the public-demo "now" view no longer crashes on installs without brand rules and never returns a developer error page.
- when the last review round fails, the harness child opens a review-blocked draft PR with its work and must-fix list instead of exiting without a result.
- every elanous-related cron line now shows up in the loop registry as a loop or an unregistered warning; none is silently dropped.
- a recorded heal event now starts the heal loop once.
- The author-depth shadow tick checks selected release-cell titles and text, holding missing-text cells with ledger receipts, without enqueueing harness work.
- brand-dependent generators now report missing rules as unmeasured rather than passing an unchecked brand assessment.
- decision cards are no longer re-sent every 20 seconds when no device is subscribed.
- a seat loop that falls back to shadow now says why.
- hq move-plan lists what a headquarters host owns before moving it.
- Each traffic tick records author-depth shadow receipts and reports held and queued-for-author counts plus incomplete ledger writes in JSON without enqueueing harness work.
- Lecture-note graph collection now OCRs photos into draft inputs, recording unreadable images with a reason.
- Lesson handbook pages show hash-free dated IDs and readable, 200-character cause and remedy summaries.
- a failed Pod run now reports why it failed instead of «no error diagnostic».
- The scheduled harness queue tick now records author-depth shadow receipts at most once every 30 minutes without changing dispatch decisions.
- Generate a capability map from maturity grades, green release cells, and the marketing feature map, with evidence gaps and patent-held concepts marked.
- the Telegram intake digest now leads with what matters to us, at most three items in a short situation-reason-action form.
- tests no longer start the real heal loop (and its paid external grounding) when they record a failure event.
- Feature maps now use marketing-map maturity, publication status, and PR citations when a row has no release checklist cell.
- seat requests can be listed and closed from the CLI.
- a waiting harness-queue item now names which seat cap is holding it back.
- seat launch caps follow each seat's remaining work and lend
- at most two heal loops run at once; further failures wait in the inbox.
- intake check now flags paid dependencies a new tool could replace, and asks for a hands-on trial first.
- agent-env capture records a secret-free profile of the local Claude, Codex and Grok setup.
- Rhythm daily dry runs preserve review files, deduplicate PR landings, and bound unlanded runs; weekly reviews use scheduled cuts and recent daily news.
- Returned Pod child logs now populate the host logs database once per job, preserving event identity and source attribution.
- A new public guide shows how to attach a Claude Code or Codex session to an elanous seat using a project-local marker and context checks.
- links saved from Telegram are absorbed right away instead of waiting for the daily run.
- the HQ arbiter asks the operations seat to promote the standby after the holder goes silent; automatic promotion stays opt-in and a failed runbook is never reported as a promotion.
- the draft sweep no longer treats two drafts as the same goal just because they share a title; it needs a matching goal id, or the same title on the same harness branch stem, and never an auto-generated file-name title.
- Idle seat checks now request the next evidence-free yellow release cell after 30 minutes, with shadow mode by default.
- test processes no longer run the real author-depth shadow on every queue tick (it timed out the seat-loop tests).
- doctor node-modules reports missing or mismatched installed packages in a working tree.
- a finished run that stalls while catching up with main is kept as harvestable instead of being dropped.
- The public loop agents guide now explains the orchestrator's handoff flow, shadow and live modes, human decision boundary, and status commands.
- the changed-file type check fails instead of passing when it cannot see TypeScript changes that are in the diff.
- a review that failed to run is no longer shown as PASS in PR comments or the PR body, and it is retried once with another provider.
- AX briefs now include the measured, deduplicated self-implement merge count and report source read failures explicitly.
- the child model provider chosen for a run is now used in Pods and local runs, or the launch is refused.
- the release checklist gate fails on a carry-over ID collision instead of silently leaving the item behind.
- several release checklist commands opening a fresh ledger at the same time no longer fail with "duplicate column name".
- one seat at its cap no longer blocks other seats' goals in the harness queue.
- draft sweeps record a daily count of old harness drafts and say why a sweep failed.
- pod run always saves the job's log to the artifact folder it announces.
- the run supervisor no longer stops a run as «no progress» when its children finished and committed on a non-main base.
- the draft cleanup and steward loops no longer fail outside a git checkout, and a failing graph step keeps the real error line.
- Pod launches now pick the pool member with the most real free capacity instead of always the first one.
- Pods no longer receive a child effort flag that `self implement` rejects, which would stop the Pod at startup.
- Pods launched at the same moment share one GitHub App token instead of each minting one, and a Pod whose GitHub login fails is retried once after a short backoff.
- every harness run records which door it came through and whether it went via the queue; eln harness doors shows the daily table.

## Security

- agent-env capture redacts key-shaped values (sk-, ghp_, AKIA… and long digit-heavy strings) even in plain identifier fields.

Plus 103 internal changes.

## Known issues

The following issues are known in this release.

- Known issues have been reported for this release.

# 0.2.14

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-14/

## Behavior changes

- `elanous hq promote --to <host>` previews the six-step HQ promotion without writing; `--apply` verifies the lease and standby checksums before copying into an isolated universe, starting nexus without MCP, and setting steward rescue; only one `--apply` runs per host at a time.
- Agent-mission DRIVE-OK no longer mistakes an `rg`, `grep`, or `diff` no-match tool exit for a failed mission when artifact evidence is verified; genuine final-answer failures still block success.
- Seat loops gain a live-safe mode (default stays shadow): it enqueues allowed goals through the harness queue with a per-item idempotency key, recovers an enqueue whose ledger row was lost to a crash, and refuses a same-key queue item carrying a different task instead of adopting it.
- `elanous release place` and `elanous release rebalance` place checklist cells by priority, merged-PR pace, seat limits and dependencies; a freeze window holds operational rollout but the release still exists and takes cells.
- Setting the ignored `ELANOUS_CONFIG_DIR` variable now prints one warning naming the config directory actually used and the `--config-dir` flag to use instead.
- the harness gate no longer treats a change to a test file plus docs as docs-only.
- `elanous loop status --all` now checks seat, cron-shell and orchestrator loops beside graph loops, uses the cron that is actually installed, and judges twice-a-day style schedules by their longest gap.
- the harness queue attributes running harness processes to seats by working tree on macOS and counts a parent and its child run once.
- a built-in YouTube summary graph turns a video transcript into a one-line verdict, key points and cards without external skills.
- when a harness run merges, older drafts of the same goal are marked superseded right away.
- the built-in YouTube summary falls back to speech-to-text when a video has no captions.
- `elanous harness goal <pr|runId>` shows the goal, run and outcome behind a harness PR in one view.
- `elanous loop list --all` shows every loop (graph, seat, cron-shell, orchestrator) in one table and warns about unregistered cron loops.
- the harness launch budget gate no longer blocks codex launches on subscription usage when the codex quota policy allows credits and a credit balance is confirmed.
- a Pod launch no longer dies when the host's grok subscription is about to expire: grok is dropped from that run's fallback chain with a warning and the run goes on with codex.
- `elanous flow tick` splits one Wish card into release cells, routes sensitive portions to owner decisions, and places safe cells with a read-only `flow plan <cardId> --dry-run` preview.
- the harness drops stale out-of-scope files that would silently revert recent main commits before committing a run's work.
- The youtube-master skill now runs on bun without tsx and says which optional engine (ffmpeg, yt-dlp, whisper) is missing instead of failing silently.
- the launch gate's duplicate-run check no longer gives up on old finished run ledgers without a goal id.
- the loop registry recognises hq-fence role wrappers and periodic elanous commands as named cron loops.
- the built-in YouTube graph can produce a study note (concepts, terms, steps and self-check questions).
- the harness gate looks at the whole run's changes before skipping tests for a source without paired tests, and flags the skip loudly.
- The "now" context view has a public-demo audience that folds internal items and hides seat codes, PR and run ids, host names and home paths.
- `harness say|ask --seat` stamps the seat into the run ledger so queue caps attribute runs correctly even outside a seat's working tree.
- the loop registry names cron jobs that run elanous via bun bin/elanous.mjs, and titles hq-fence wrapped lines by their inner command.
- the daemon's "now" endpoint serves a public-demo audience and enforces it in demo mode.
- the harness gate always runs the maturity-table tests when a change registers a slash, bot or CLI command.
- Pod harness kubectl calls no longer die with ENOBUFS on large cluster listings during OOM retry decisions.
- the loop registry recognises absolute-path eln cron jobs (including the loop checker itself) and never silently drops an elanous-related cron line.
- `elanous harness goal archive` previews finished goal documents and, with `--apply`, copies them to an indexed state archive and lists the repository files to remove in a PR (it never deletes or commits repository files).
- goal archive matches run ledgers by run id instead of absolute paths, and can optionally trust a goal document's own finished-run record.
- harness incident records name the entrance, seat, host and a redacted output tail, and burst warnings say whose burst it was.

Plus 129 internal changes.

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-13/

## Behavior changes

- Seat packs export seat charters, referenced loop graphs, verdicts and default budgets with a SHA-256 manifest after a pre-write public-leak check.

- `elanous agent-mission duo` runs Codex and Claude Code concurrently in separate worktrees, groups their PTY decisions by mission, and compares evidence and DRIVE-OK outcomes.
- Git test helpers and deterministic children clear inherited repository-location variables; the runner restores and fails on shared core.bare changes.
- A release gate judges completed Pod shards, including zero-test file errors, when a retried shard remains silent, recording its files as environment stalls and testing each once on the host.
- Release publish tests now use real auto-approval output, accepting added warning-only rows while rejecting missing blocking metrics.
- The internal ops feed installs tag-local frozen dependencies when the tag and main differ, instead of building the tagged PWA with main's dependencies.
- Telegram `아크:` messages create a daemon-backed fabric plan draft with step previews and approval/edit buttons; execution remains gated on approval.
- Hold host Pod leases from goal authoring until the Job's Pod is Running or terminal, and show authoring reservations separately from waiting Jobs and running Pods.
- Persona YAML now names each coworker's todo file; `elanous persona loop <name> --once` records the priority-and-deadline pick in shadow without executing it.
- `elanous steward readiness --since 24h [--json]` reads shadow-tick decisions, hypothetical actions, planning cost estimates and human-confirmation counts without changing state.
- Steward graph node processes now persist triage and schedule decisions to logs.db for `elanous logs` queries without changing routing.
- `elanous team validate <file>` checks a YAML team definition, persona references, and acyclic handoffs without running the team.
- TC records an ask-shadow in the existing seat ask ledger when its release judgment finds another seat's red cell, without dispatching a message.
- HQ fencing now prefers a host-local identity file over replicated config, fails closed on a damaged identity file, reports mismatches, and provides `elanous hq host set <name>` to write it.
- Ledger-writing release checklist and decisions CLI commands now respect the HQ lease generation, with an observed override and pre-lease bootstrap allowance.
- omni-crawl and omni-digest start with bun instead of npx tsx — about ten times faster to start and no download on a fresh machine — and say plainly which optional engine is missing.
- steward digest is sent as an operations report, not a trading report.
- Decision cards now open with a 30-second pitch — situation, problem, question, answer, the recommendation, one alternative, who cross-checked it and any dissent.

# 0.2.12

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-12/

## Behavior changes

- `elanous release checklist add` warns about an ID used in another release and requires `--allow-duplicate-id` to proceed; a blocked move now identifies the destination cell.
- CLI and cron outbound sends now register a standalone log-store sink, recording bot identity, kind, source, delivery path, outcome and body length without message text or credentials.
- `elanous persona add <name> --from <preset>` creates one editable YAML persona; `persona edit --set` validates fields and returns exit 2 with a one-line reason for unknown keys.

- Harness launches warn and proceed when provider usage is unmeasured; only measured exhaustion blocks the launch.
- When a change has more than 30 caller tests, the gate keeps the ones closest to it — tests naming a route on a changed line, then direct importers nearest in the directory tree — instead of the alphabetically first; the overflow still runs in the release-cut sweep.
- Retry a silent release-gate Pod shard once in a fresh Pod before reporting it stalled.
- the release loop now packs the internal ops feed from the release tag (a fresh checkout with the web UI built), so operations hosts receive exactly the released code instead of whatever main held at that moment.
- Harness runs and external agent missions publish fail-soft claimed and done events with run and PR references to the context journal.
- Market review bundles exclude plugin runtime and graph-run state while retaining the private-content leak gate for authored files.
- Persist ordered agent-mission PTY decisions to logs.db so the PWA inside scene can replay them.
- when a harness change edits a test, the gate again also runs the changed sources' co-located and related tests (a narrowing that ran only the edited test is reverted).

# 0.2.11

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-11/

## Behavior changes

- Add a bounded context journal for Claude Code hooks, Codex agent missions, and harness child lifecycle events.
- Workflow runs now support single-node execution, resuming from prior runs, and pin-required test mode.
- Decision-card answers now resume the waiting harness run, while deadlines retain safe fallback behavior.
- two programs writing to the same conversation at once no longer lose messages from its count or undo its project assignment; assigning a conversation to a project that does not exist now answers «not found» (404), and the dashboard suggests a project from the session folder whenever it changes.
- The INSIDE2 live-event SSE endpoint (`GET /v1/inside/events`) streams graph, harness, seat, steward, and PTY decision updates with secret values masked.
- Steward live mode launches eligible goals only after pre-launch duplicate, budget and location checks, while money, publishing and security decisions still require human approval.
- Add a rate-limited diagnostics intake endpoint that stores doctor bundles in private S3 and returns a support code.
- The elanous-basics plugin now includes a Google Workspace skill for your own Gmail and Calendar, plus Drive and Sheets reads.
- A new elanous-essentials pack bundles five everyday skills — YouTube digests, web search and crawling, link digests, diagrams and lecture-note digitizing — each with a free path and a bring-your-own-key path.
- `elanous harness stop <run>` now finds and stops a run that was launched from another worktree: the run is bound to its process in a per-user host registry, and the stop still checks the process start time before any signal.
- Pod pool members can use separate registry ports, and lease checks exclude members whose in-Pod DNS lookup fails.
- Setup automatically enables skills for signed-in `gh`, `gws`, `op`, and `himalaya` CLIs, skips unavailable or signed-out CLIs, and keeps public GitHub repository reads available without signing in.
- Plugin make now researches the web and Aside local memory before drafting a connector, skill, and graph, and continues when research is unavailable.
- workflows can run independent nodes in parallel (`concurrency`, default 1) and route a failed node to an `on_error` handler instead of stopping.
- Condense a day of context events and decisions into source-linked, project-and-seat memory with correction, conflict and retirement signals.
- Install, list and remove YAML team sets of titled personas with validated handoffs.
- Pods have a lite tier (2 GiB) you opt into: `elanous pod run --lite` runs network-skill commands (omni-crawl, omni-digest) on a small image, and `--pod-memory lite` or a `Pod 메모리: lite` goal line gives a harness goal 2 GiB; a lite run that runs out of memory retries once on the high tier, and `pod lease status` shows lite slots.
- `elanous graph variant <template> --plan <json> --dry-run|--run` validates a variant, saves its graph beside the run ledger, and executes the validated wiring.
- The harness gate runs up to 30 reverse-import and HTTP-route consumer tests, including PWA tests for removed routes, and warns with the full overflow list.
- `elanous make "<one-line request>"` classifies the request and routes it to the existing plugin maker or workflow builder, asking which to use when classification fails.
- Isolate provider availability tests from host credentials and verify Codex-first selection with the default fallback chain.
- Plugin make can prepare a leak-checked official-market bundle after local installation, with an optional configured signature and no publishing.
- `elanous skills install essential --code <CODE> --email <address> --agree` installs the essential skill pack from a gift code — nothing is sent without `--agree`, existing skill folders are never overwritten, and an oversized or mismatched download is refused.
- Asking how X reacts to something now searches X itself, so the answer cites x.com posts.
- Delegated work now picks a default output for each task — a report, slides, a research doc or a post draft — instead of ending in a chat answer, and what was produced is recorded in one outputs list.
- Cache successful per-member DNS checks for ten minutes under a host lock and exclude labeled DNS probe Pods from goal counts.
- the harness launch gate no longer blocks every launch when the launch universe's config has no model chain: it judges with the built-in default chain and prints a warning, and an explicit `--child-llm-provider` counts as the chain.
- classification calls no longer fail when no global LLM provider is configured: a role that names its own provider resolves without one, and an injected classifier transport still runs (marked unresolved).

Plus 206 internal changes.

# 0.2.10

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-10/

## Behavior changes

- Tools started from the Telegram bot (such as event video) find node and Homebrew even when the bot runs as a background service.
- `elanous harness stop` accepts the short run id shown in output and stops that run's pod jobs too.
- Release checklist entries written by an older build to checklist.json are picked up again instead of being ignored.
- Creating a worktree for a large repository no longer times out after 30 seconds, and a timeout is reported clearly instead of ending at a progress line.
- `elanous harness stop` finds a run's launcher process even when the orchestrator record is missing, and says what it looked at instead of reporting «no process».
- `elanous update --restart` no longer restarts the service when the same build is already installed.
- Windows: elanous no longer crashes on start (a Linux-only library was loaded at import), and the PowerShell installer keeps the system PATH after installing Bun and adds elanous to the user PATH so a new window finds it.
- Send a business card photo to the Telegram bot and get a summary, an approach strategy and a follow-up draft back in the same chat (nothing is sent); a photo without a caption starts this only when the photo looks like a business card, and a keyword like «business card», «strategy» or «email draft» starts it right away and picks just that part.
- `elanous seat loop --seat <SEAT> --once` picks a seat's next assigned item and records what it would do (shadow by default · off unless configured), and `elanous seat report` summarises the day.
- Operational reports (schedule health, retros, memory review, repo watch) no longer fall through to a different bot's chat when no channel is mapped for them.
- Ask elanous where the release stands or tell it to add an item or move a release date; changes ask you once before they are made.
- In web app chat, an approval sheet appears before a write or shell tool runs: allow once, always allow for this session, or deny; with no answer in 60 seconds nothing runs.
- Drag a file onto the web app chat to see a «drop here to attach» overlay, and paste a screenshot to attach it.
- The web app menu is grouped into Today · Chats · Work · Create · Library · Settings.
- An unknown `/command` in web app chat is no longer sent to the model; you are told it is unknown or not yet supported in the web app.
- Reopening or reattaching the web terminal no longer leaves a black screen; earlier output and new output both show.
- In the terminal chat box, Ctrl+C clears what you typed, and pressing it twice on an empty box exits.
- When a pod run ends, the harness says why (stopped, supervisor verdict, left a PR) instead of claiming it never reached the pod.
- The steward can launch scheduled harness goals on pods in parallel under a budget gate, raising human decisions for money, publishing or security, and reporting each landing back — shadow mode first.
- Web app chat shows your conversations in a list on the left with «+ New chat» and search; on a phone the list opens as a drawer.
- The first time you run `eln`, it starts the engine and shows a browser setup link (and opens the browser when a display is available); `elanous setup --terminal` keeps setup in the terminal.
- «Assign to COO» in the web app: approve or hold a posting right in the request, play result videos and images in place, and see each result's sources.
- «Field upload» in the web app shows the event folder's count and finished reel as soon as it opens (including uploads from other devices), shows why a reel failed, and says up front which picked files are left out (over 20, over 100 MB, or over 250 MB in total).
- The web app sends a push notification when a request you assigned finishes, fails, or waits for your approval; tapping it opens that request.
- Reopening an earlier web chat shows each message at the time it was sent, not the time you opened it.
- On narrow screens (phones, a folded Fold) the web app's top bar shrinks to one line with the rest under «⋯», and the web terminal opens full screen on touch devices.
- On narrow screens the web terminal's three toolbar rows shrink to one line (terminal name · connection dot · «⋯» with every action).
- When an assigned document draft fails its check, elanous rewrites it once with the reviewer's note before giving up.
- On phones and a folded Fold, the web app has bottom tabs (Today · Chats · Work · Create · More).
- An assigned task that finished now shows its result in the web app even when the graph wrote its file in its own run folder or only answered in text, and a failed task shows the step's actual reason.
- On first run, if a phone is on the same Wi-Fi, elanous also prints a one-time link (and a QR code when available) to continue setup from the phone, and over SSH it prints the one `ssh -L` line to open setup from your own computer.
- A request sent to the Telegram bot as a directive now gets its result back in the same chat when the work finishes: the produced file, or a link and one-line summary.
- Settings has a «Try experimental features» switch; turn it on to see features still in beta, marked `실험` (experimental).
- Add `즉석` (or `instant`) after `#현장` in a Telegram caption to get the quicker field reel that reuses pre-made intro and end cards; `telegram.fieldReelMode` sets the default.
- In the web first-run setup you can sign in with your ChatGPT subscription right there — in the browser on the same computer, or with a device code from a phone — without going back to the terminal.
- The web app now says `대화` (conversation) instead of `세션` (session) in the conversation picker, its ID pill and the delete dialog, and the delete dialog says plainly that it cannot be undone.
- In web app chat you can keep typing while a reply streams; your next messages queue as chips and send in order.
- Assigned tasks can now use event photos and the field feed, take attached files, and a plain question is answered by the seat instead of failing with «no installed graph fits».
- The one-line installer no longer stops on a fresh root Ubuntu (WSL, containers) for want of unzip, curl or git: as root with apt it installs them itself (`--no-install-deps` to opt out); other users still get the one-line hint.
- In the terminal app, messages you type while a reply is streaming now appear in the chat log when they are sent, in order.
- In web app chat, once you deny a write or shell tool the assistant stops asking for the same tool again in that reply, and the approval wait time can be set with acp.toolApproval.timeoutMs.
- In chat, a short fact question is answered from a web search with sources, instead of opening the shell and browser and running out of time.
- `elanous nexus status` no longer sends its local health check through an HTTP proxy, so it reports a running daemon correctly on machines with a proxy set.
- In web app chat, `/sessions` lists your recent conversations and `/resume <first characters>` picks one up again.
- In web app chat, `/model <tier>` shows or sets the model tier (unknown values are not saved), and `/provider` and `/reasoning` point you to the matching settings.
- The web app's Today screen shows approvals waiting for you, your five most recent requests and your five most recent conversations.
- Web app chat can group conversations into projects: pick a project from the switcher, or create your first one when you have none.

Plus 184 internal changes.

# 0.2.8

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-8/

When something is in the way, Elanous now tells you why and fixes what it can, right there.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash   # one line
```

or `npm install -g elanous`.

## New

- **Unreadable skills no longer stop the first screen.** If a skill file from another tool can't be read, you see "N skills could not be read". After you confirm, Elanous repairs only what it can and keeps the original.
- **Clear sign-in where a browser can't open.** Over ssh or on a machine without a screen, Elanous no longer tries to open a browser; it says why and what to do instead. At the machine itself, ChatGPT sign-in opens in the browser directly.
- **One language.** First-run setup and sign-in text now use one language.
- **`elanous doctor`** finds local LLMs on this machine, such as Ollama and LM Studio. **`elanous doctor --bundle`** writes one diagnostics file with secrets redacted, which you can send when asking for help.
- **Bring over what you already use.**
  - `elanous import` shows the skills and MCP servers it found in agents you already use, such as Claude Code and Codex.
  - `elanous import --apply` brings them in. Skills stay where they are and are not copied; MCP servers arrive switched off.
  - `elanous import --undo` reverts the import in one step.
  - Secrets and sign-ins are not moved.
  - `elanous connect claude` hooks up the skills of an agent you already use in one step.
- **Telegram and Discord bots carry over.** First-run setup finds your existing Telegram and Discord bot settings and shows them. It brings them over only if you agree, and token values are never shown.
- **Decisions in your DMs.** When Elanous needs a person to decide, it asks with button cards in a Telegram or Discord DM. It asks twice before anything that can't be undone.
- **Web terminal.** Opening a terminal in the web app no longer freezes for a few seconds the first time, and tabs in the background stop refreshing.
- **Error reports.** When an error happens, Elanous sends only the error, the version and a random install ID to the operators. It sends no name or email.
  - Reports are deleted automatically after 30 days.
  - You are told on first run.
  - One line turns it off: `elanous config set errorReports.enabled false`.
- **Docs** now mark each screen as stable or experimental. A new guide shows how to put a single HTML page online with Vercel.

## Experimental

- After you upload event photos and the vertical video is made, an Instagram feed draft is prepared on its own and waits in "Pending posts". Nothing is posted until a person taps "Final post".

Plus 92 internal changes.

# 0.2.6

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-6/

## New

- `elanous plugin make "<request>"` writes a local graph plugin from one sentence, checks its shape, installs it and can run it right away (`--run`).
- The terminal dashboard now tells you when Elanous was updated underneath it and asks you to restart it.
- Nodes from installed plugins now appear in the web workflow editor's palette without restarting the daemon, even when no MCP server is configured.

## Fixes

- Running several `elanous ask` commands at the same time no longer fails or loses sessions from the session list.
- `elanous ask --json` prints only JSON on standard output, including on machines where no notification channel is set up.
- `elanous harness stop` finds a run's launcher process even when the orchestrator record is missing, and says what it looked at instead of reporting «no process».

Plus 75 internal changes.

## Known issues

0.2.6 ships with a few known issues. None of them affect installing with the one-line installer, starting or updating Elanous, running the harness, or your data. Fixes are planned for the next release.

- If you install with `npm i -g elanous`, install Bun first — on a machine without Bun the `elanous` command cannot start in this release. The one-line installer is not affected; it sets up Bun for you.
- Two more marketer plugins, card-followup and video-explainer, are not in the official market yet. They will be listed in a follow-up update.
- A few internal checks in our own test suite fail in this release. They do not change how Elanous behaves.

# 0.2.3

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-3/

A shorter command (`eln`), a web app tab to approve and merge, tasks from Linear and other tools, several machines working as one, and a lighter terminal UI.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash   # one line
```

npm had not been updated for 0.2.3; the one-line installer above is the way to install this release.

## Read this first — behaviour changes

- **Tailnet devices paste a token once.** Header-based same-origin trust now applies only to the browser on the daemon's own machine (a direct loopback connection with no proxy in front). A phone or laptop that opens the web app through the tailnet link pastes its token once; the "not connected" banner names the exact setting.
- **Short command `eln`.** `eln` is installed next to `elanous`; the old `mda` alias is gone. An existing `eln` that is not ours is never overwritten.
- **`elanous schedule migrate|adopt|release|delete` show what they would do** by default. Add `--yes` to apply.
- **`elanous task` / `elanous tasks` manage the task manager's tasks** (`list · show · approve`) instead of printing a retirement notice.
- **Tasks from outside wait for your approval.** Tasks that arrive from Linear, a webhook or another agent are queued as waiting; rules under `tox.external.autoRun` can run some automatically.
- **Harness runs on Kubernetes pods merge only after the same checks pass on the host machine**, so a change that is green only on Linux no longer reaches `main`. A run stopped by a provider, quota or credential problem keeps its branch and does not open a draft pull request.
- **Saved Telegram links** — up to 30 more a day are absorbed, separately from the daily cap of 10.
- **Obsidian** — when no vault is configured, elanous looks in `~/Documents/Obsidian`.
- **The web app can merge.** The new Approvals tab has a merge button; it works only with the owner token.
- **The terminal UI is one essential layout.** The rich layout, virtual windows and their commands and tools are gone. A config that still sets `dashboard.uiMode` loads without error.

## New

- **Approvals tab** in the web app (after Intake): the summary, files and checks of a pull request waiting for approval, a direct link `/approvals?pr=<n>`, and approve-and-merge. On an installed copy, set the repository once: `elanous config set intake.approvals.repo <owner>/<name>`.
- **Tasks from other tools** — a Linear connector (`elanous connector linear set-key | sync | set-webhook-secret`; the Basic plan is enough), an intake endpoint `POST /v1/tasks`, and `elanous tasks list · show · approve`. An approved `[dev]` task runs through the harness; other tasks go to an agent with tools. See [Tasks and intake](/using-elanous/tasks-and-intake).
- **Several machines** — give each machine an id, the duties it takes and its rank for a seat (`elanous machine set | show`); hand the coordinator seat over or let a lower-ranked machine take it when the holder stops (`elanous role handoff | accept | watch | status`); machines without a daemon join as light members. See [Multi-machine setup](/operations/multi-machine).
- **Other agents can use elanous** — an MCP tool `elanous_task_submit`, running an elanous agent over MCP and collecting its result, and each ACP session's own working folder. A Claude Code plugin is included as a preview (`claude --plugin-dir integrations/elanous-agent`).
- **Web terminal** — open an agent's terminal from a link (`elanous agent-mission` prints it on its first lines; harness runs print a `[surface-link]` line), a single input path, and reopening a terminal id attaches to the live shell instead of starting another one.
- **Web chat** — the first message is no longer lost when a session is adopted, slash commands run on Enter, and controls that did nothing are gone.
- **Intake** — one box in the web app with a live preview of how the text is read; the same classifier on every surface; a Telegram link saved as a note is marked absorbed so the daily run does not absorb it again.
- **Costs** — one-off model calls (classification, summaries) are recorded with a role; `elanous usage runs --by role`.
- **Workflows** — webhook signature checks (`auth: hmac`) and a `task` node that files a task.
- **Harness** — `elanous harness stop <runId>` stops a run's process and its pod jobs; `--pod-memory high` gives a pod run more memory (goals that touch the web app get it automatically).
- **Agent missions** — `elanous agent-mission capabilities` shows each coding CLI's MCP servers, connectors and login state; when you take over the terminal, the mission waits instead of stopping.
- **Skills** — `omni-digest` (summarise a link, post or file) ships with elanous. It needs an xAI API key; describing images and video frames also needs `AWS_S3_BUCKET`.
- **Voice** — the free voice fallback uses only programs that are installed (`edge-tts`, macOS `say`).

## Security

- The MCP endpoint no longer trusts a loopback connection that came through a proxy (for example `tailscale serve`).
- See the tailnet token change above.

## Documentation

New and updated pages: [Multi-machine setup](/operations/multi-machine), [Tasks and intake](/using-elanous/tasks-and-intake), [Recommended programs](/getting-started/recommended-programs), [Web app](/surfaces/pwa), [Terminal](/surfaces/pwa-terminal), [Chat](/surfaces/pwa-chat), [Graph engineering](/concepts/graph-engineering).

---

# 0.2.2

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-2/

Security hardening for the local daemon, a simpler rule for which environment a command runs in, web setup for chat bots, and a lighter, safer install.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash   # one line
```

npm had not been updated for 0.2.2; the one-line installer above is the way to install this release.

## Security

- The daemon no longer hands out its admin token over HTTP. `connect-info` returns no token; a new device pastes its token once.
- Every `/v1` route now requires authentication by default. Previously a few read routes (including the notes vault search) and several settings/control writes could be reached without a token.
- Telegram and Discord bot tokens are stored once, in the secrets store, and referenced from config — no more plaintext tokens in `config.json`.
- Isolated (test) environments no longer receive copies of production secrets: plaintext secret fields are stripped, outbound credentials (chat bot tokens, web-push keys) are left out of the copied secrets file, and copies are written `0600`.
- `elanous doctor` reports configuration and secret files that other users could read, and `elanous doctor --fix --yes` tightens them (the folder to `700`, files lose group/other bits; nothing is read).

## Changes

- **Which environment am I in?** The rule is now: an explicit root (`--test`, `--config-dir`, `ELANOUS_STATE_DIR`) wins; otherwise the installed copy is production and any source checkout is an isolated environment. The old "leader tree" setting is gone. `elanous where` shows the answer and why.
- **Web setup** — connect Telegram and Discord bots from the web app (token check, secrets store, allowed users), pick the Obsidian vault and skills, and choose the answer depth. A device that is not yet connected now says so once instead of failing silently.
- **Install and update** — installing or updating from a source checkout builds the web app first and stops if the build fails, so the installed web app always matches the code.
- **Test daemons never take production ports.** A test daemon started without `--port` leases a port from the test band; production ports are never chosen.
- **Resource coordinator (preview)** — `elanous control serve` runs a small coordinator that answers "where is this resource running?" (`elanous resources list|where`), bound to loopback or a tailnet address, with per-machine scoped tokens.
- **Codex accounts** — the shared `default` account is used only up to 60% by default (a stricter global threshold still wins), and rotation moves to the next account with room.
- **Intake** — a daily intake pipeline collects items (videos, saved Telegram messages, trending GitHub repositories), queues them with a daily cap, and absorbs them into notes.
- Many fixes found by installing on bare Ubuntu 26.04 and macOS machines.

## Notes

- If you set `dashboard.uiMode` or used `--rich`, they still load without error; the terminal UI is being simplified to a single essential layout in upcoming releases.

---

# 0.2.1

Source: https://docs.elanous.ai/releases/0-2-1/

A security fix for S3 storage, fixes found by installing on a bare Ubuntu 26.04 machine, and options that are now simply on.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash   # one line
```

npm had not been updated for 0.2.1; the one-line installer above is the way to install this release.

## S3 storage: no default bucket

Up to 0.2.0, S3 features (session backup, memory archive, metrics and others) fell back to a built-in bucket name when you had not set one. That bucket belongs to the project and allows public reads, so this was never the right default.

- **There is no default bucket any more.** Without configuration nothing is uploaded — features keep working locally.
- Two buckets, set in `~/.elanous/config.json` (or the environment):

```json
{ "storage": { "s3": { "bucket": "my-private-bucket", "publicBucket": "my-public-bucket" } } }
```

| key | environment | used for |
|---|---|---|
| `storage.s3.bucket` | `AWS_S3_BUCKET` | everything private: sessions, memory archive, metrics |
| `storage.s3.publicBucket` | `AWS_S3_PUBLIC_BUCKET` | only features that hand out public links: publishing, morning report, debug bundle |

- Keep `bucket` private (block public access). Only `publicBucket` should be publicly readable.

## Fixes from a bare Ubuntu 26.04 install

- **`/harness ask` in the TUI now actually starts the run in your project.** It printed «run launched» but the background run could not find elanous's own entry script outside the elanous source tree and exited silently.
- **The TUI harness on a repository without a git remote** now finishes on a local worktree branch instead of failing at the pull-request step (it tells you so in one line). Pass the completion flags yourself on the CLI if you really want a PR.
- **Your repository stays clean**: the `.elanous/` folder elanous creates inside a project (debug logs, goal documents) is added to that repository's local `.git/info/exclude` — your `.gitignore` is not touched.
- **No more «no crontab for …» in the middle of the TUI** on machines without a crontab.
- **Queued input shows how to take it back**: `⏳ … · Ctrl+↑ 되꺼내기`. Inside tmux, enable extended keys first: `tmux set -s extended-keys always`.
- Setup wizard: the provider line no longer names old models, and «recommended» is shown once.

## Options that are now always on

These had been on in practice for months; the switches are gone and `elanous doctor` lists them as keys you can delete:

- `instance.treeDerivedTest` — a non-leader checkout runs in its own test state; a fresh install with no leader is unaffected.
- `tools.selfImplement.selfResolveClarifications` — `elanous self author` answers its own clarification questions from repository evidence, as `harness ask/say` already did.
- `ACP_PERSIST_MODE`, `ACP_BG_SWEEP_MODE`, `PWA_VOICE` environment switches and `prEvidenceArtifactEnforce` — removed; the enabled behaviour (or observation) stays.

## Also

- `elanous graph run <file> [--dry-run]` · `elanous graph status <id>` — walk an operations graph whose nodes run registered recipes.

[Release page](https://github.com/ElanvitalAI/elanous/releases/tag/v0.2.1)
